claim: Mortality from breast cancer is almost exclusively a result of tumor metastasis.
source: Mortality from breast cancer is almost exclusively a result of tumor metastasis, and lungs are one of the main metastatic sites.
evidence: This is a statement presented in the abstract without specific experimental data or citations in this sentence, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: Lungs are one of the main metastatic sites for breast cancer.
source: Mortality from breast cancer is almost exclusively a result of tumor metastasis, and lungs are one of the main metastatic sites.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Fibroblasts in lung metastases are transcriptionally dynamic and plastic.
source: We demonstrate that fibroblasts in lung metastases are transcriptionally dynamic and plastic, and reveal stage-specific gene signatures that imply functional tasks, including extracellular matrix remodeling, stress response, and shaping the inflammatory microenvironment.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data analysis showing differential gene expression patterns across metastatic stages.

claim: Fibroblasts in lung metastases exhibit stage-specific gene signatures related to extracellular matrix remodeling.
source: We demonstrate that fibroblasts in lung metastases are transcriptionally dynamic and plastic, and reveal stage-specific gene signatures that imply functional tasks, including extracellular matrix remodeling, stress response, and shaping the inflammatory microenvironment.
evidence: This is supported by pathway enrichment analysis and RNA-seq data showing ECM-related genes differentially expressed across stages.

claim: Fibroblasts in lung metastases exhibit stage-specific gene signatures related to stress response.
source: We demonstrate that fibroblasts in lung metastases are transcriptionally dynamic and plastic, and reveal stage-specific gene signatures that imply functional tasks, including extracellular matrix remodeling, stress response, and shaping the inflammatory microenvironment.
evidence: This is supported by pathway enrichment analysis showing stress response genes enriched in MIF.

claim: Fibroblasts in lung metastases exhibit stage-specific gene signatures related to shaping the inflammatory microenvironment.
source: We demonstrate that fibroblasts in lung metastases are transcriptionally dynamic and plastic, and reveal stage-specific gene signatures that imply functional tasks, including extracellular matrix remodeling, stress response, and shaping the inflammatory microenvironment.
evidence: This is supported by pathway enrichment analysis showing inflammatory genes enriched in MAF.

claim: Myc is a central regulator of fibroblast rewiring during metastatic progression.
source: Furthermore, we identified Myc as a central regulator of fibroblast rewiring and found that stromal upregulation of Myc transcriptional networks is associated with disease progression in human breast cancer.
evidence: This is supported by multiple bioinformatics analyses (STRING, ANAT, RegNetwork, VarElect) and functional validation experiments.

claim: Stromal upregulation of Myc transcriptional networks is associated with disease progression in human breast cancer.
source: Furthermore, we identified Myc as a central regulator of fibroblast rewiring and found that stromal upregulation of Myc transcriptional networks is associated with disease progression in human breast cancer.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of human breast cancer patient data (GSE14548) showing MYC expression correlates with tumor grade.

claim: The microenvironment is crucial in supporting metastases formation.
source: It is increasingly appreciated that in addition to tumor cell-intrinsic survival and growth programs, the microenvironment is crucial in supporting metastases formation (Erez and Coussens, 2011; Obenauf and Massagué, 2015; Quail and Joyce, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The role of the metastatic microenvironment and the molecular crosstalk between stromal cells at the metastatic niche are poorly characterized.
source: Nevertheless, while years of research have revealed the central role of the microenvironment in supporting tumor growth and response to therapy at the primary tumor site (Quail and Joyce, 2013; Hanahan and Coussens, 2012; Albini et al., 2018), the role of the metastatic microenvironment and the molecular crosstalk between stromal cells, including fibroblasts and immune cells at the metastatic niche, are poorly characterized.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field, supported by citations indicating what is known about primary tumors versus metastases.

claim: Secreted factors and extracellular vesicles from tumor and stromal cells instigate a permissive pre-metastatic niche by influencing the recruitment and activation of immune cells.
source: Secreted factors and extracellular vesicles from tumor and stromal cells were reported to instigate a permissive pre-metastatic niche by influencing the recruitment and activation of immune cells (Deng et al., 2012; Peinado et al., 2011; Qian et al., 2011; Coffelt et al., 2015; Quail et al., 2017), and by modifying the composition of the extracellular matrix (ECM) (Erler et al., 2009; Malanchi et al., 2012; Oskarsson et al., 2011; Oskarsson and Massagué, 2012; Nielsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Secreted factors and extracellular vesicles from tumor and stromal cells instigate a permissive pre-metastatic niche by modifying the composition of the extracellular matrix.
source: Secreted factors and extracellular vesicles from tumor and stromal cells were reported to instigate a permissive pre-metastatic niche by influencing the recruitment and activation of immune cells (Deng et al., 2012; Peinado et al., 2011; Qian et al., 2011; Coffelt et al., 2015; Quail et al., 2017), and by modifying the composition of the extracellular matrix (ECM) (Erler et al., 2009; Malanchi et al., 2012; Oskarsson et al., 2011; Oskarsson and Massagué, 2012; Nielsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Various immune cell populations are functionally important in facilitating breast cancer pulmonary metastasis.
source: Various immune cell populations were shown to be functionally important in facilitating breast cancer pulmonary metastasis (Coffelt et al., 2015; Albrengues et al., 2018; DeNardo et al., 2009; Fridlender et al., 2015; Jablonska et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Very little is known about the role of fibroblasts during the complex process of metastases formation.
source: However, very little is known about the role of fibroblasts during the complex process of metastases formation.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Cancer-associated fibroblasts are a heterogeneous population of fibroblastic cells found in the microenvironment of solid tumors.
source: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are a heterogeneous population of fibroblastic cells found in the microenvironment of solid tumors.
evidence: This is established knowledge about CAFs.

claim: In breast carcinomas, CAFs are the most prominent stromal cell type.
source: In some cancer types, including breast carcinomas, CAFs are the most prominent stromal cell type, and their abundance correlates with worse prognosis (Liu et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: CAF abundance correlates with worse prognosis in breast carcinomas.
source: In some cancer types, including breast carcinomas, CAFs are the most prominent stromal cell type, and their abundance correlates with worse prognosis (Liu et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: CAFs play a novel role in mediating tumor-promoting inflammation in mouse and human carcinomas.
source: We previously demonstrated a novel role for CAFs in mediating tumor-promoting inflammation in mouse and human carcinomas (Erez et al., 2013; Erez et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the authors' prior work.

claim: Profound changes in the expression of pro-inflammatory genes occur in fibroblasts isolated from metastases-bearing lungs.
source: Importantly, we found profound changes in the expression of pro-inflammatory genes in fibroblasts isolated from metastases-bearing lungs (Raz et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Comprehensive profiling of metastasis-associated fibroblasts in spontaneous metastasis was not previously done.
source: However, comprehensive profiling of metastasis-associated fibroblasts in spontaneous metastasis was not previously done.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field.

claim: αSMA expression is upregulated in metastases-bearing lungs compared to normal lungs.
source: Notably, analysis of αSMA and FSP-1 indicated an upregulation in the expression of these markers in metastases-bearing lungs (Figure 1B, C), suggesting that lung metastases are associated with fibroblast activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescent staining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: FSP-1 expression is upregulated in metastases-bearing lungs compared to normal lungs.
source: Notably, analysis of αSMA and FSP-1 indicated an upregulation in the expression of these markers in metastases-bearing lungs (Figure 1B, C), suggesting that lung metastases are associated with fibroblast activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescent staining data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Lung metastases are associated with fibroblast activation.
source: Notably, analysis of αSMA and FSP-1 indicated an upregulation in the expression of these markers in metastases-bearing lungs (Figure 1B, C), suggesting that lung metastases are associated with fibroblast activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the upregulation of fibroblast activation markers αSMA and FSP-1.

claim: The number of fibroblasts is significantly increased in macrometastatic lungs compared to normal lungs.
source: Flow cytometric analysis of normal lungs as compared with lungs of tumor-bearing mice revealed significantly increased numbers of fibroblasts in macrometastatic lungs (Figure 1E, F).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Fibroblasts are both activated and increase in numbers in the metastatic microenvironment of breast cancer lung metastasis.
source: Thus, fibroblasts are both activated and increase in numbers in the metastatic microenvironment of breast cancer lung metastasis.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the immunostaining and flow cytometry data presented.

claim: Macrometastasis-associated fibroblasts are strikingly different from normal lung fibroblasts.
source: Initial data analysis indicated that fibroblasts isolated from lungs with macrometastases (macrometastasis-associated fibroblasts [MAFs]) were strikingly different from Normal lung fibroblast (NLF) as well as from fibroblasts isolated from lungs with micrometastases (micrometastasis-associated fibroblasts [MIFs]) (Figure 1H, I, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by PCA and hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 1H and I.

claim: Macrometastasis-associated fibroblasts are strikingly different from micrometastasis-associated fibroblasts.
source: Initial data analysis indicated that fibroblasts isolated from lungs with macrometastases (macrometastasis-associated fibroblasts [MAFs]) were strikingly different from Normal lung fibroblast (NLF) as well as from fibroblasts isolated from lungs with micrometastases (micrometastasis-associated fibroblasts [MIFs]) (Figure 1H, I, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by PCA and hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 1H and I.

claim: The MIF fraction contains a mixture of normal, non-metastasis-associated fibroblasts as well as metastasis-associated fibroblasts.
source: Notably, since fibroblasts were isolated from entire lungs, rather than from specific metastatic lesions, the MIF fraction contained a mixture of normal, non-metastasis-associated fibroblasts as well as metastasis-associated fibroblasts.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental design where fibroblasts were isolated from whole lungs.

claim: Initial data analysis did not reveal significant differences between NLF and MIF.
source: As a result, initial data analysis did not reveal significant differences between NLF and MIF.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the initial analysis.

claim: Metastasis-associated fibroblasts are not only functionally activated but also transcriptionally reprogrammed.
source: Thus, metastasis-associated fibroblasts are not only functionally activated but also transcriptionally reprogrammed.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the RNA-seq data showing differential gene expression.

claim: The MAF group clusters separately from NLF and MIF based on differentially expressed genes.
source: Expectedly, hierarchical clustering based on these genes revealed that the MAF group clustered separately from NLF and MIF (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The expression pattern in MIF is distinct from both MAF and NLF gene expression.
source: Interestingly, we found that the expression pattern in MIF was distinct from both the MAF and the NLF gene expression, including genes that had opposite changes in MAF vs. MIF, suggesting that they are activating a distinct transcriptional program (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: MIF activates a distinct transcriptional program.
source: Interestingly, we found that the expression pattern in MIF was distinct from both the MAF and the NLF gene expression, including genes that had opposite changes in MAF vs. MIF, suggesting that they are activating a distinct transcriptional program (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is inferred from the distinct expression patterns observed in MIF.

claim: The MIF group clusters separately from both NLF and MAF based on differentially expressed genes.
source: Indeed, hierarchical clustering based on these differentially expressed genes confirmed that the MIF group clustered separately from both NLF and MAF (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Only a small number of differentially expressed genes are shared across different metastatic stages.
source: Interestingly, only a small number of these genes were shared across the different stages, suggesting again that each stage is defined by its own specific gene signature (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Each metastatic stage is defined by its own specific gene signature.
source: Interestingly, only a small number of these genes were shared across the different stages, suggesting again that each stage is defined by its own specific gene signature (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is inferred from the limited overlap of differentially expressed genes between stages.

claim: Principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering separate each of the metastatic stages.
source: Accordingly, principal component analysis (PCA) and hierarchical clustering applied on the selected gene signature dataset separated each of the metastatic stages (Figure 2E, F).
evidence: This claim is supported by PCA and hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: MIF activates a unique stage-specific transcriptional program.
source: Thus, although the transcriptional changes in fibroblasts isolated from micrometastases may have been masked by the presence of normal fibroblasts in this fraction, further analyses suggested that MIF, as well as MAF, activates a unique stage-specific transcriptional program.
evidence: This is inferred from the distinct clustering and gene expression patterns observed in MIF.

claim: MAF activates a unique stage-specific transcriptional program.
source: Thus, although the transcriptional changes in fibroblasts isolated from micrometastases may have been masked by the presence of normal fibroblasts in this fraction, further analyses suggested that MIF, as well as MAF, activates a unique stage-specific transcriptional program.
evidence: This is inferred from the distinct clustering and gene expression patterns observed in MAF.

claim: The differentially expressed genes per comparison have significantly more interactions than expected.
source: We found that per comparison the differentially expressed genes had significantly more interactions than expected (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), suggesting that they are functionally related.
evidence: This claim is supported by protein-protein interaction analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The differentially expressed genes are functionally related.
source: We found that per comparison the differentially expressed genes had significantly more interactions than expected (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), suggesting that they are functionally related.
evidence: This is inferred from the significant protein-protein interactions observed.

claim: Gene expression signatures in fibroblasts isolated from the micrometastatic stage are highly and specifically enriched for functions related to cellular response to stress.
source: Interestingly, we found that gene expression signatures in fibroblasts isolated from the micrometastatic stage were highly and specifically enriched for functions related to cellular response to stress, including Hsf1 activation, heat shock response, and response to unfolded protein (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by pathway enrichment analysis results.

claim: Upregulated genes in MIF related to stress and protein folding include several heat shock proteins: Hspa8, Hsp90aa1, Hspd1, Hspe1.
source: Upregulated genes in MIF that were related to stress and protein folding included several heat shock proteins: Hspa8, Hsp90aa1, Hspd1, Hspe1, and others (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: ECM remodeling terms are enriched in both MIF and MAF.
source: ECM remodeling terms were enriched in both MIF and MAF (Figure 3B), indicating the central importance of ECM modifications in facilitating metastasis.
evidence: This claim is supported by pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: ECM modifications are centrally important in facilitating metastasis.
source: ECM remodeling terms were enriched in both MIF and MAF (Figure 3B), indicating the central importance of ECM modifications in facilitating metastasis.
evidence: This is inferred from the enrichment of ECM remodeling pathways across metastatic stages.

claim: ECM remodeling is operative throughout the metastatic process.
source: Notably, while ECM remodeling was operative throughout the metastatic process, the specific genes related to ECM remodeling in the different metastatic stages were distinct (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by pathway enrichment analysis showing ECM terms in both MIF and MAF.

claim: The specific genes related to ECM remodeling in different metastatic stages are distinct.
source: Notably, while ECM remodeling was operative throughout the metastatic process, the specific genes related to ECM remodeling in the different metastatic stages were distinct (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Gene expression signatures in fibroblasts isolated from macrometastases are highly enriched for inflammation-related pathways.
source: Gene expression signatures in fibroblasts isolated from macrometastases were highly enriched for inflammation-related pathways (Figure 3B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Genes related to inflammation including many chemokines and cytokines are upregulated specifically in MAF.
source: Indeed, analysis of enriched pathways revealed that genes related to inflammation including many chemokines and cytokines were upregulated specifically in MAF (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Functions related to inflammatory responses, including TNFα and IL-6 signaling, are enriched in MAF.
source: Similar to the results obtained in our previous analyses, we found that functions related to inflammatory responses, including TNFα and IL-6 signaling, were enriched in MAF (Figure 3F, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA results shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Myc target genes are the most highly and significantly enriched in both metastatic stages.
source: Interestingly, we found that Myc target genes were the most highly and significantly enriched in both metastatic stages (Figure 3G, Supplementary file 2), suggesting that this transcription factor (TF) may play a central role in the functional molecular co-evolution of metastasis-associated fibroblasts.
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA results shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Myc may play a central role in the functional molecular co-evolution of metastasis-associated fibroblasts.
source: Interestingly, we found that Myc target genes were the most highly and significantly enriched in both metastatic stages (Figure 3G, Supplementary file 2), suggesting that this transcription factor (TF) may play a central role in the functional molecular co-evolution of metastasis-associated fibroblasts.
evidence: This is inferred from the high enrichment of Myc target genes across metastatic stages.

claim: The transcriptome of lung fibroblasts is rewired during metastatic progression.
source: Taken together, these findings imply that the transcriptome of lung fibroblasts is rewired during metastatic progression, driving changes in the expression of distinct molecular pathways.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the RNA-seq and pathway analysis data.

claim: Transcriptional changes in ECM remodeling are evident at early stages of metastases formation.
source: Moreover, the transcriptional changes in ECM remodeling and stress response, which represent potential metastases-promoting tasks, are evident at early stages of metastases formation, suggesting that fibroblasts play an important role already at the onset of the metastatic process.
evidence: This is based on the observation that ECM-related genes are enriched in MIF.

claim: Transcriptional changes in stress response are evident at early stages of metastases formation.
source: Moreover, the transcriptional changes in ECM remodeling and stress response, which represent potential metastases-promoting tasks, are evident at early stages of metastases formation, suggesting that fibroblasts play an important role already at the onset of the metastatic process.
evidence: This is based on the observation that stress response genes are enriched in MIF.

claim: Fibroblasts play an important role already at the onset of the metastatic process.
source: Moreover, the transcriptional changes in ECM remodeling and stress response, which represent potential metastases-promoting tasks, are evident at early stages of metastases formation, suggesting that fibroblasts play an important role already at the onset of the metastatic process.
evidence: This is inferred from the early activation of metastasis-promoting pathways in MIF.

claim: Five candidate transcription factors were enriched in at least one analysis and in at least one metastatic stage: Hif1a, Hsf1, Myc, Nfkb1, and Stat3.
source: Analysis of TFs terms within the results identified five candidate TFs that were enriched in at least one analysis and in at least one metastatic stage: Hif1a, Hsf1, Myc, Nfkb1, and Stat3 (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of transcription factor enrichment in pathway and GSEA results.

claim: Hsf1 is only enriched in the micrometastatic stage versus normal lungs.
source: We found that Hsf1 was only enriched in the micrometastatic stage vs. normal lungs, and Hif1a was enriched only in the macrometastatic stage vs. normal lungs.
evidence: This claim is based on transcription factor enrichment analysis.

claim: Hif1a is enriched only in the macrometastatic stage versus normal lungs.
source: We found that Hsf1 was only enriched in the micrometastatic stage vs. normal lungs, and Hif1a was enriched only in the macrometastatic stage vs. normal lungs.
evidence: This claim is based on transcription factor enrichment analysis.

claim: Nfkb1 is enriched in the macrometastatic stage compared with both normal and micrometastases.
source: Nfkb1 and Stat3 were enriched in the macrometastatic stage compared with both normal and micrometastases.
evidence: This claim is based on transcription factor enrichment analysis.

claim: Stat3 is enriched in the macrometastatic stage compared with both normal and micrometastases.
source: Nfkb1 and Stat3 were enriched in the macrometastatic stage compared with both normal and micrometastases.
evidence: This claim is based on transcription factor enrichment analysis.

claim: Only Myc is enriched in all three comparisons (MIF vs. NLF, MAF vs. NLF, MAF vs. MIF).
source: Notably, only Myc was enriched in all three comparisons (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This claim is based on transcription factor enrichment analysis.

claim: In MAF gene signature, Stat3 has the largest number of connections in STRING analysis, closely followed by Myc.
source: In MAF gene signature, Stat3 had the largest number of connections, closely followed by Myc.
evidence: This claim is based on STRING protein-protein interaction analysis.

claim: In MIF gene signature, Myc has the largest number of connections in STRING analysis.
source: In MIF gene signature, Myc had the largest number of connections (Figure 4A, orange).
evidence: This claim is based on STRING protein-protein interaction analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Myc has the largest number of direct connections in all comparisons in ANAT analysis.
source: Analysis of the results revealed that Myc had the largest number of direct connections in all comparisons and is overall connected to the fibroblast metastasis-associated gene signatures with the shortest path and with the highest centrality in all comparisons (Figure 4A, yellow, Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1[1–3]).
evidence: This claim is based on ANAT pathway analysis shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: Myc is connected to the fibroblast metastasis-associated gene signatures with the shortest path in all comparisons.
source: Analysis of the results revealed that Myc had the largest number of direct connections in all comparisons and is overall connected to the fibroblast metastasis-associated gene signatures with the shortest path and with the highest centrality in all comparisons (Figure 4A, yellow, Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1[1–3]).
evidence: This claim is based on ANAT pathway analysis shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: Myc has the highest centrality in the fibroblast metastasis-associated gene network in all comparisons.
source: Analysis of the results revealed that Myc had the largest number of direct connections in all comparisons and is overall connected to the fibroblast metastasis-associated gene signatures with the shortest path and with the highest centrality in all comparisons (Figure 4A, yellow, Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1[1–3]).
evidence: This claim is based on ANAT pathway analysis shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: Myc plays a central role in mediating the transcriptional rewiring of fibroblasts in the lung metastatic niche across different stages.
source: These results suggested that Myc plays a central role in mediating the transcriptional rewiring of fibroblasts in the lung metastatic niche across the different stages.
evidence: This is inferred from the multiple network analyses showing Myc's centrality.

claim: Myc has the greatest number of targets in all comparisons in RegNetwork analysis.
source: We found that Myc had the greatest number of targets in all comparisons, followed by Stat3 and Nfkb1 (Figure 4A, green).
evidence: This claim is based on RegNetwork analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Myc has the highest number of connections and the highest average score for both directly and indirectly related genes in all comparisons in VarElect analysis.
source: In agreement with previous analyses, Myc had the highest number of connections and the highest average score for both directly and indirectly related genes in all comparisons (Figure 4A, pink, Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is based on VarElect analysis shown in Figure 4A and 4C.

claim: Myc achieves significantly higher scores than all other transcription factors in all three gene signatures.
source: The results indicated that Myc achieved significantly higher scores than all other TFs in all three gene signatures (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is based on comparative statistical analysis of TF rankings shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Some fibroblasts co-express several transcription factors (MYC, STAT3, NFKB1, HSF1).
source: Analysis revealed that while some of the fibroblasts co-expressed several TF (Figure 4E, solid boxes), other subpopulations expressed only MYC (Figure 4E, dashed boxes).
evidence: This claim is based on multiplex immunofluorescent staining shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Some fibroblast subpopulations express only MYC.
source: Analysis revealed that while some of the fibroblasts co-expressed several TF (Figure 4E, solid boxes), other subpopulations expressed only MYC (Figure 4E, dashed boxes).
evidence: This claim is based on multiplex immunofluorescent staining shown in Figure 4E.

claim: MYC is expressed in fibroblasts in both micro- and macrometastases.
source: Moreover, we found that MYC is expressed in fibroblasts in both micro- and macrometastases.
evidence: This claim is based on multiplex immunofluorescent staining data.

claim: Myc is involved in many biological processes, including cell growth and proliferation, cell stemness, and metabolism.
source: Myc (myelocytomatosis oncogene) is a TF involved in many biological processes, including cell growth and proliferation, cell stemness, and metabolism.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Myc function.

claim: Myc is deregulated in many human cancers.
source: Myc is deregulated in many human cancers and is known to play an important role in the pathogenesis of cancer, particularly in cancer cells (Dang, 2012; Poole and van Riggelen, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Myc plays an important role in the pathogenesis of cancer, particularly in cancer cells.
source: Myc is deregulated in many human cancers and is known to play an important role in the pathogenesis of cancer, particularly in cancer cells (Dang, 2012; Poole and van Riggelen, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Myc is significantly upregulated in macrometastases-associated fibroblasts.
source: Analysis of the results indicated that Myc is significantly upregulated in macrometastases-associated fibroblasts (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Myc target genes Hspe1, Hsp90aa1, Odc1, and Fosl1 are upregulated in fibroblasts isolated from lungs with metastases.
source: The results indicated that these Myc targets were upregulated in fibroblasts isolated from lungs with metastases (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Control fibroblasts highly upregulate the expression of Myc in response to tumor cell-secreted factors.
source: Importantly, control fibroblasts highly upregulated the expression of Myc in response to tumor cell-secreted factors (Figure 5C, left bars), while Myc inhibition abrogated the upregulation of Myc in response to tumor cell-secreted factors in activated fibroblasts (Figure 5C, right bars).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Myc inhibition abrogates the upregulation of Myc in response to tumor cell-secreted factors in activated fibroblasts.
source: Importantly, control fibroblasts highly upregulated the expression of Myc in response to tumor cell-secreted factors (Figure 5C, left bars), while Myc inhibition abrogated the upregulation of Myc in response to tumor cell-secreted factors in activated fibroblasts (Figure 5C, right bars).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Fibroblasts at the primary tumor site are reprogrammed by tumor cell-derived paracrine signaling.
source: Fibroblasts at the primary tumor site were previously shown to be reprogrammed by tumor cell-derived paracrine signaling (Sharon et al., 2015; Jin et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Tumor-derived factors activate multiple CAF-associated functions including enhanced motility in wound healing assay.
source: Incubation of isolated primary lung fibroblasts with CM from Met-1, a PyMT-derived breast carcinoma cell line (Borowsky et al., 2005), or from 4T1 cells, a model of triple-negative breast cancer, indicated that tumor-derived factors activated multiple CAF-associated functions including enhanced motility in wound healing assay (Figure 5—figure supplement 1[1–4]) and increased contraction of collagen gel matrices (Figure 5—figure supplement 1[5–7]).
evidence: This claim is supported by wound healing assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Tumor-derived factors activate increased contraction of collagen gel matrices in lung fibroblasts.
source: Incubation of isolated primary lung fibroblasts with CM from Met-1, a PyMT-derived breast carcinoma cell line (Borowsky et al., 2005), or from 4T1 cells, a model of triple-negative breast cancer, indicated that tumor-derived factors activated multiple CAF-associated functions including enhanced motility in wound healing assay (Figure 5—figure supplement 1[1–4]) and increased contraction of collagen gel matrices (Figure 5—figure supplement 1[5–7]).
evidence: This claim is supported by collagen contraction assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Normal lung fibroblasts are reprogrammed by signaling from breast cancer cells, resulting in acquisition of tumor-promoting properties.
source: Thus, NLFs are reprogrammed by signaling from breast cancer cells, resulting in acquisition of tumor-promoting properties.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the functional assay data.

claim: siMyc fibroblasts are less contractile than control fibroblasts.
source: We found that siMyc fibroblasts were less contractile and exhibited significantly attenuated migration capacity as compared with controls (Figure 5E–H, Figure 5—figure supplement 1[8–9]).
evidence: This claim is supported by collagen contraction assay data shown in Figure 5E-F.

claim: siMyc fibroblasts exhibit significantly attenuated migration capacity compared to control fibroblasts.
source: We found that siMyc fibroblasts were less contractile and exhibited significantly attenuated migration capacity as compared with controls (Figure 5E–H, Figure 5—figure supplement 1[8–9]).
evidence: This claim is supported by wound healing assay data shown in Figure 5G-H.

claim: The changes in fibroblast contractility and migration due to Myc knockdown are not related to effects of Myc on fibroblast proliferation.
source: Notably, these changes were not related to any effects of Myc on fibroblast proliferation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1[10, 11]).
evidence: This claim is supported by proliferation assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Scratch wound closure is significantly enhanced by overexpression of Myc in a proliferation-independent manner.
source: Interestingly, analysis of CAF-like functions revealed that scratch wound closure was significantly enhanced by overexpression of Myc in a proliferation-independent manner (Figure 5J, Figure 5—figure supplement 1[12]).
evidence: This claim is supported by wound healing assay data shown in Figure 5J and proliferation data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Myc overexpression induces upregulation of its target genes BCAT1 and ODC1.
source: Notably, Myc overexpression induced upregulation of its target genes BCAT1 and ODC1, which were also upregulated in MAF.
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data.

claim: Multiple pro-inflammatory genes are upregulated by Myc overexpression.
source: Moreover, multiple pro-inflammatory genes were upregulated by Myc overexpression (Figure 5K).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5K.

claim: Myc and NFKB1 share target genes.
source: Myc itself is a target of NFKB1 (Grumont et al., 2004; La Rosa et al., 1994), and the two TFs share target genes (Han et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Myc is a target of NFKB1.
source: Myc itself is a target of NFKB1 (Grumont et al., 2004; La Rosa et al., 1994), and the two TFs share target genes (Han et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Overexpression of Myc is sufficient to activate CAF-like functions including wound closure and expression of its target genes.
source: Thus, overexpression of Myc was sufficient to activate CAF-like functions including wound closure and expression of its target genes, as well as pro-inflammatory signaling in fibroblasts.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the Myc overexpression experiments.

claim: Overexpression of Myc is sufficient to activate pro-inflammatory signaling in fibroblasts.
source: Thus, overexpression of Myc was sufficient to activate CAF-like functions including wound closure and expression of its target genes, as well as pro-inflammatory signaling in fibroblasts.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the Myc overexpression experiments.

claim: Myc has a central role in enhancing fibroblast activation.
source: Taken together, our findings imply that Myc has a central role in enhancing fibroblast activation and in mediating their acquisition of metastasis-promoting functions.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the Myc knockdown and overexpression experiments.

claim: Myc has a central role in mediating fibroblast acquisition of metastasis-promoting functions.
source: Taken together, our findings imply that Myc has a central role in enhancing fibroblast activation and in mediating their acquisition of metastasis-promoting functions.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the Myc knockdown and overexpression experiments.

claim: MYC is upregulated in breast cancer stroma in correlation with disease progression, as reflected by pathological grade.
source: Importantly, analysis revealed that MYC is upregulated in breast cancer stroma in correlation with disease progression, as reflected by pathological grade: expression of MYC was significantly elevated in the stroma of grade 3 tumors compared with stroma isolated from more differentiated tumors (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of human patient data (GSE14548) shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Expression of MYC is significantly elevated in the stroma of grade 3 tumors compared with stroma isolated from more differentiated tumors.
source: Importantly, analysis revealed that MYC is upregulated in breast cancer stroma in correlation with disease progression, as reflected by pathological grade: expression of MYC was significantly elevated in the stroma of grade 3 tumors compared with stroma isolated from more differentiated tumors (Figure 6A).

claim: NFKB1 does not exhibit a grade-dependent trend of expression in breast cancer stroma.
source: Interestingly, NFKB1 and STAT3 did not exhibit this grade-dependent trend of expression (Figure 6B, C).

claim: Stromal expression of MYC is positively correlated with stromal expression of multiple target genes in human breast cancer patients.
source: We found that stromal expression of MYC was positively correlated with stromal expression of multiple target genes (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis of human patient data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Among the MYC downstream target genes positively correlated with its expression in human patients are HSP90AA1, HSPD1, ODC1, and HSPE1.
source: Notably, among the MYC downstream target genes that were positively correlated with its expression in human patients were several of the genes that were also validated in murine lung fibroblasts: HSP90AA1, HSPD1, ODC1, and HSPE1 (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1), suggesting that stromal MYC-driven gene signatures play a functional role in human breast cancer.
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Stromal MYC-driven gene signatures play a functional role in human breast cancer.
source: Notably, among the MYC downstream target genes that were positively correlated with its expression in human patients were several of the genes that were also validated in murine lung fibroblasts: HSP90AA1, HSPD1, ODC1, and HSPE1 (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1), suggesting that stromal MYC-driven gene signatures play a functional role in human breast cancer.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between MYC and its target genes in human breast cancer stroma.

claim: MYC is expressed in a subset of lung metastasis-associated stromal cells in human breast cancer patients.
source: We found that MYC was expressed in a subset of lung metastasis-associated stromal cells (Figure 6E), suggesting that stromal upregulation of MYC plays a functional role in human lung metastasis.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry staining of human lung metastases shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Stromal upregulation of MYC plays a functional role in human lung metastasis.
source: We found that MYC was expressed in a subset of lung metastasis-associated stromal cells (Figure 6E), suggesting that stromal upregulation of MYC plays a functional role in human lung metastasis.
evidence: This is inferred from the expression of MYC in stromal cells of human lung metastases.

claim: The activation of MYC transcriptional networks in the stroma of breast tumors plays a role in tumor aggressiveness in human breast cancer.
source: These results suggest that the activation of MYC transcriptional networks in the stroma of breast tumors plays a role in tumor aggressiveness in human breast cancer.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the human patient data analysis.

claim: Integration of multiple analytical platforms of gene expression, connectivity, and function provides powerful insight on functional and temporal regulation of the dynamic transcriptome of fibroblasts in lung metastasis.
source: In summary, we show that integration of multiple analytical platforms of gene expression, connectivity, and function provided a powerful insight on functional and temporal regulation of the dynamic transcriptome of fibroblasts in lung metastasis.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the methodological approach used in the study.

claim: Myc is a novel regulator of fibroblast metastases-promoting properties.
source: We uncovered central molecular pathways that drive the activation of growth-promoting tasks in fibroblasts via known regulators of CAF tumor-promoting activities including Myc, a novel regulator of fibroblast metastases-promoting properties.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the study's findings about Myc's role in fibroblasts.

claim: The study elucidates the dynamic transcriptional co-evolution of fibroblasts during the multistage process of breast cancer metastasis.
source: Our findings elucidate for the first time the dynamic transcriptional co-evolution of fibroblasts during the multistage process of breast cancer metastasis.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the overall contribution of the study.

claim: Hsf1 was previously shown to be upregulated in CAFs in breast and lung cancers.
source: Hsf1 was previously shown to be upregulated in CAFs in breast and lung cancers and to drive a stromal tumor-promoting transcriptional program that correlated with worse prognosis (Scherz-Shouval et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Hsf1 was recently implicated in mediating the transition from chronic inflammation to colon cancer by mediating ECM remodeling.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Activation of Hsf1 transcriptional regulation in fibroblasts occurs during the early stages of metastasis.
source: Our findings expand these observations to the metastatic microenvironment and show that activation of Hsf1 transcriptional regulation in fibroblasts occurs during the early stages of metastasis and thus may play a role in instigating tumor-promoting functions in metastasis-associated fibroblasts.
evidence: This is based on the observation that Hsf1-related pathways are enriched in MIF.

claim: Hsf1 may play a role in instigating tumor-promoting functions in metastasis-associated fibroblasts.

claim: ECM components and remodeling facilitate breast cancer metastasis to lungs.
source: Indeed, ECM components and remodeling were demonstrated to facilitate breast cancer metastasis to lungs, and pancreatic cancer metastasis to liver (Malanchi et al., 2012; Oskarsson et al., 2011; Nielsen et al., 2016; Cox et al., 2013; Yuzhalin et al., 2018; Alexander and Cukierman, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: ECM components and remodeling facilitate pancreatic cancer metastasis to liver.

evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Transcriptional rewiring of fibroblasts to mediate collagen synthesis and ECM organization is a central function of metastasis-associated fibroblasts.
source: We show that transcriptional rewiring of fibroblasts to mediate collagen synthesis and ECM organization is a central function of metastasis-associated fibroblasts, which is instigated early during the metastatic process and persists during advanced metastatic disease.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the pathway enrichment analysis showing ECM-related genes across stages.

claim: CAFs play a central role in mediating tumor-promoting inflammation at the primary tumor site.
source: CAFs are known to play a central role in mediating tumor-promoting inflammation at the primary tumor site (Servais and Erez, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Activation of inflammation is implicated in shaping of the metastatic microenvironment.
source: Importantly, activation of inflammation was also implicated in shaping of the metastatic microenvironment (Coffelt et al., 2015; Quail et al., 2017; Albrengues et al., 2018), but the role of fibroblasts in mediating inflammation at the metastatic site is only recently emerging: recent studies implicated CAF-derived cytokines including IL-1β, IL-33, and CXCL9/10 in promoting breast cancer lung metastasis (Pein et al., 2020; Ershaid et al., 2019; Shani et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: CAF-derived cytokines including IL-1β, IL-33, and CXCL9/10 promote breast cancer lung metastasis.

source: While the importance of Myc in promoting cell transformation and tumorigenesis is well established (Poole and van Riggelen, 2017), its role in the tumor stroma is largely uncharacterized.

claim: Inhibition of Myc attenuates tumor-promoting functions of fibroblasts.
source: Indeed, inhibition of Myc attenuated tumor-promoting functions of fibroblasts and overexpression of Myc was sufficient to induce these functions, confirming that Myc functionally contributes to fibroblast acquisition of tumor-promoting traits.

source: Indeed, inhibition of Myc attenuated tumor-promoting functions of fibroblasts and overexpression of Myc was sufficient to induce these functions, confirming that Myc functionally contributes to fibroblast acquisition of tumor-promoting traits.

source: Taken together, these findings indicate that in addition to its known role in driving carcinogenesis in tumor cells, Myc functions in stromal rewiring in the tumor microenvironment in both primary tumors and metastases of breast cancer.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the study's findings in both mouse models and human patients.
